findings.description: The integrity check now counts index entries rather than files present on disk. git ls-files continues listing tracked files after they have been deleted from the working tree.
findings.failure_mode: Deleting a tracked System Zone script or hook leaves ACTUAL_COUNT unchanged, so preflight passes the count comparison despite an incomplete installation. The previous filesystem count detected this deletion.
findings.suggested_fix: Count tracked paths that actually exist in MANIFEST_TREE, or explicitly check tracked manifest paths for missing files before accepting the count.

findings.description: In a submodule mount (.loa/.claude is a directory) the new branch reclassifies every absent manifest path as informational 'not-mounted' whenever the same path exists under .loa/. Because the upstream submodule always contains every manifest path, the 'Missing' failure can never fire in submodule mode. Deleting a linked System Zone file (e.g. a hook or gate script symlink) is now indistinguishable from a by-design unlinked path and no longer fails the check.
findings.failure_mode: A removed .claude/ guard script in a submodule-mounted repo passes check-loa.sh with 'Integrity verified', weakening the tamper detector the three-zone model relies on.
findings.suggested_fix: Compare against the mount's intended link set (the mount-scope manifest that tools/check-manifest-paths.sh / check-loa-mount-scope.bats appear to own) rather than mere existence under .loa/: a path that is in the intended set but absent should still be 'Missing'.

findings.description: The function previously ended with `[[ "$drift" == "false" ]] && log ...`, so it returned non-zero when drift was detected. The new unconditional `return 0` makes the function always succeed. If any caller (or `set -e` propagation) relied on the return status rather than on a counter maintained by fail(), tamper detection no longer affects the script's exit code.
findings.failure_mode: Tampered or Missing files are printed but check-loa.sh exits 0 if the exit status is derived from the function's return value.
findings.suggested_fix: Return 1 when drift=true (`[[ "$drift" == "false" ]]` as the last statement, or explicit `if` / `return`), or confirm fail() increments a global that drives the final exit and document that here.

findings.cross_file_justification: codex-headless.extra.cli_model now points here, and .claude/adapters/tests/test_pricing_resolution_ladder.py asserts the hop prices through this entry; ablation-row.sh sums ledger_cost_usd into runs.jsonl cost_usd.
findings.description: gpt-6.1-sol pricing is an acknowledged placeholder copied from gpt-5.5, yet it is the rate every codex-headless hop estimate and MODELINV row now resolves to. Ledger rows will carry pricing_source=config with no marker that the rate is provisional, so the ablation cost_usd column and any spend reports mix confirmed and placeholder rates indistinguishably.
findings.failure_mode: Cost comparisons across arms that use the codex hop are computed on an unverified rate card and cannot be told apart from confirmed pricing after the fact.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a machine-readable flag on the entry (e.g. pricing.provisional: true) that the ledger propagates (pricing_provisional), or gate the entry behind the Sprint 258 bead so the rate is confirmed before rows are written.

findings.description: The row builder copies phase fields name, model_requested and models_used straight from meta/pipeline.json with no defaults, but the script's own --validate requires name:string, model_requested:string and models_used:object. A phase that errored before any model invocation (infrastructure_error, interrupted) or a bare arm that lacks these keys produces a row that --validate rejects, even though the builder exited 0.
findings.failure_mode: runs.jsonl written by ablation-row.sh fails ablation-row.sh --validate on its own output, breaking the batch runner's validation step.
findings.suggested_fix: Default the required phase fields in the builder (`models_used: (.models_used // {})`, `model_requested: (.model_requested // "")`, `name: (.name // .label // "")`) or relax the validator to match what pipeline-run.sh guarantees.

findings.description: The header refuses to take the arm from sandbox/ (DEC-0413) because the agent under test can write there, but degraded, degraded_reason and voices_run are derived from sandbox/grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-1/adversarial-*.json, which the same agent can write or edit. A run can therefore present itself as non-degraded with full voice counts regardless of what the gates actually did.
findings.failure_mode: Degraded-run filtering in the ablation analysis trusts agent-writable artifacts, so a mis-shaped or tampered envelope hides a degraded gate.
findings.suggested_fix: Prefer the harness-owned copy under eval/ (already the fallback) and only consult sandbox/ when eval/ is absent, or cross-check envelope voice counts against MODELINV rows in eval/model-invoke.jsonl and flag a mismatch as degraded.

findings.cross_file_justification: The diff modifies several files under .claude/ (check-loa.sh, preflight.sh, generated-model-maps.sh, defaults/model-config.yaml, bridgebuilder dist) but .claude/checksums.json is not in the diff or the omitted-file list.
findings.description: If .claude/checksums.json is tracked, every modified .claude/ file in this change will hash-mismatch against it and check_integrity will report 'Tampered' for each on the next run. Only model-config.yaml.checksum was regenerated.
findings.failure_mode: check-loa.sh fails with multiple Tampered lines immediately after merge until the manifest is regenerated.
findings.suggested_fix: Run tools/gen-checksums.sh as part of this change (or confirm the manifest is generated only at release/mount time and is not tracked).
